opinions: The U.S. has a lot of influence
I see challenges here at home—like underfunded schools, infrastructure needs, and political division—that make me wonder how sustainable our global role is if we don't invest more in our own people
I believe a country's strength starts with how well it educates its children and supports its communities
I'm not convinced America's role in the world is ending anytime soon
Manufacturing has been hollowed out here in Pennsylvania, and that weakens our economic foundation
We rely too much on other countries for critical goods
politically, we seem more divided than ever
both parties are more interested in fighting each other than solving real problems
I still believe in American resilience
Our military is strong
our economy is still the largest in the world
we've got innovative people and companies

If we can get back to making things here, restore some common sense in Washington, and focus on our own interests without overextending ourselves overseas, I think we'll be leading for a long time yet
The U.S. still plays a huge role in the world, especially in medicine and technology
Many [doctors and researchers from all over] still look to the U.S. for leadership in healthcare innovation
I worry about our country sometimes—the political divisions, the healthcare system struggling to serve everyone, the way we handle crises
If the U.S. wants to stay strong, we need to take better care of our people here at home first
The U.S. still leads in innovation, venture capital, and software ecosystems
the gap is narrowing in fields like AI, quantum computing, and semiconductor manufacturing
The U.S. position feels less unilateral than it did in the 1990s or early 2000s
we're already in a transitional phase toward a more multipolar world
predicting an 'end date' feels like trying to predict a market crash—you know indicators are there, but timing is nearly impossible
The resilience of U.S. institutions, the dollar, and cultural influence might prolong this phase longer than some expect
I don't think anyone can give you a precise date
the idea of American 'hegemony,' that singular, dominant leadership we've had since the end of the Second World War, is already evolving
It's not so much about it coming to a crashing 'end' on a Tuesday afternoon, but about it being reshaped
The world is becoming multipolar
these are all factors
we have our own internal struggles to contend with
these things weaken our ability to project a consistent and confident vision abroad
A nation needs to be strong at home to lead effectively overseas
will there be a day when we wake up and America is no longer the leading power? Probably not
there may well be a day, perhaps in my granddaughter's lifetime, when it's simply one of several major centers of power in a more crowded, complicated world
The task, I believe, is to manage that transition wisely, with grace and principle, rather than fear it
We need to focus on being a good neighbor on the global stage
